layering: CANONICAL DECISION: Adopt Proposal #1's LAYER-GROUPED hexagon (technical-axis: domain/ ports/ adapters/ services/ controllers/ infra/ composition/) as the file-tree backbone because it (a) literally matches the user's mandate 'Controller -> Service -> Port -> Adapter, wired by a composition root', (b) keeps the file count and the single composition root simpler than #2's two-tier per-slice roots, (c) preserves the user's existing orchestrator/backstop/ path + pavo/router.py convention. IMPORT from Proposal #2 (the genuinely better ideas): PHI-as-a-type (RedactedText newtype the egress ports structurally require), Money/SolDeadline integer-cents value objects for triage, the tamper-evident audit chain + cost ledger modeled as SHARED ports every service consumes (not re-implemented per feature), and an explicit domain state-machine on the Appeal aggregate (DENIED->TRIAGED->IN_APPEAL->AWAITING_SIGNOFF->FILED/ABANDONED) so the cross-feature pipeline is encoded as aggregate transitions, NOT slice-to-slice service calls.

Six layers, strict one-way dependency (a layer may import only layers below it; adapters never import services/controllers; domain imports nothing): L1 domain (pure entities, value objects, enums, errors, RedactedText, triage/routing pure math) -> L2 ports (abstract Protocol/ABC interfaces + their request/result DTOs; the ONLY thing services depend on) -> L3 adapters (real + sim implementations of one port each; real adapters own all vendor SDK/HTTP; sim adapters do REAL local work) and infra (config, http client, db engine, logging, security headers) -> L4 services (use-cases; depend ONLY on ports + domain + an injected Clock/IdGen) -> L5 controllers (FastAPI HTTP/WS edge; depend on services via DI; never construct anything) -> composition root (the ONE impure wiring file graph: reads Settings, builds every adapter by mode, assembles services, returns an immutable Container; owns the FastAPI lifespan).

PAVO exception to real/sim symmetry: RoutingPort is the one capability whose composition factory has a real (torch) and a sim (numpy) adapter that are POLICY-IDENTICAL (bit-faithful: verified 0/2000 argmax mismatches, 1.9e-6 max logit error against the live checkpoint) — the numpy adapter is NOT a degraded fake, it is the same frozen policy on a torch-free backend, usable as production fallback AND test double. PAVO weights/policy are frozen: adapters wrap inference only, never call .train(), never alter turn_to_state_vector defaults or the 48->3 collapse thresholds.

PHI redaction boundary is structural, not conventional: every egress port (LetterRenderPort, EventBusPort/WS, AuditLogPort, FileStorePort, TtsPort, ReasoningPort outbound, RetrievalPort outbound) accepts ONLY domain.redacted.RedactedText for its PHI-bearing fields. A service cannot hand raw str to an egress port without first passing it through RedactionPort (TrueFoundry), which is the sole producer of RedactedText. This makes the six PHI-leak Critical/High vulns a type error at the boundary, with runtime defense-in-depth assertions in each egress adapter.

The only file permitted to read os.environ is infra/config.py (a frozen pydantic-settings Settings). The only files permitted to import a vendor SDK/torch/httpx are the real adapters + infra/http_client.py + the PAVO adapters. An architecture guard test (tests/arch/test_layering.py) statically asserts both invariants so the global-state-coupling and single-LLM-chokepoint rules cannot silently regress.

Async-first hot path: the per-turn loop (CallService) and swarm fan-out (SwarmService) are fully async; the concurrency cap (ConcurrencyGatePort) is acquired per-appeal via 'async with gate.slot(appeal_id)'; the appeal repo lock is held only across in-memory dict/row mutation (never across an await to a vendor), so routing/retrieval/reasoning happen lock-free — fixing the lock-scope-serializes-the-swarm and threadpool-starvation vulns.

persistence.decision: Replace the in-memory global APPEALS dict with SQLite (WAL mode) behind AppealRepositoryPort + AuditLogPort + CostLedgerPort. Sim/test uses bounded-LRU+TTL in-memory adapters that honor the SAME contract (atomic CAS, append-only). SQLite is the production default (single-node, file-backed, sufficient for a hackathon RCM tool; DATABASE_URL allows Postgres later without touching services).
persistence.engine: aiosqlite / sqlite3 WAL via infra/db.py; one writer connection, atomic transactions; row caps + TTL eviction job for ephemeral state.

schema.appeals: id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, status TEXT NOT NULL (DENIED|TRIAGED|IN_APPEAL|AWAITING_SIGNOFF|FILED|ABANDONED), payer_id TEXT, member_id_hash TEXT (salted hash, never raw), claim_number_hash TEXT, denial_json TEXT (redacted DenialExtraction), recoverable_cents INTEGER, sol_deadline TEXT (ISO), route_decision TEXT, needs_human_review INTEGER, created_at TEXT, updated_at TEXT, version INTEGER (optimistic-lock for update_status_atomic CAS). INDEX(status), INDEX(sol_deadline), INDEX(needs_human_review).
schema.events: id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, appeal_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES appeals(id), seq INTEGER NOT NULL, ts TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT (denial_parsed|turn_routed|evidence_retrieved|line_composed|contradiction_found|letter_drafted|nurse_claimed|signed|filed), payload_json TEXT (RedactedText only), provenance_json TEXT. UNIQUE(appeal_id, seq). Append-only — the per-appeal evidence timeline.
schema.audit: id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, appeal_id TEXT, stage TEXT, model TEXT, mode TEXT (real|sim), ts TEXT, prompt_sha256 TEXT, completion_sha256 TEXT, redaction_count INTEGER, prompt_tokens INTEGER, completion_tokens INTEGER, usd_micros INTEGER, gateway_request_id TEXT, prev_hash TEXT NOT NULL, record_hash TEXT NOT NULL. prev_hash = record_hash of the prior row (hash-chained, tamper-evident); verify_chain() walks and recomputes. Append-only, no UPDATE/DELETE.
schema.cost_ledger: id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, appeal_id TEXT, stage TEXT, vendor TEXT (truefoundry|qwen), model TEXT, prompt_tokens INTEGER, completion_tokens INTEGER, chars INTEGER, usd_micros INTEGER, ts TEXT. INDEX(appeal_id). Aggregated by snapshot()/cost_to_date(); usd stored as integer micros (no float).
schema.signoffs: appeal_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES appeals(id), nurse_id TEXT, letter_sha256 TEXT, signature_b64 TEXT (Ed25519), public_key_id TEXT, audit_chain_head TEXT (record_hash at sign time), signed_at TEXT. One row per filed appeal; insert is gated on verify_chain()==True.
schema.review_queue: appeal_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES appeals(id), priority INTEGER, claimed_by TEXT NULL, claimed_at TEXT NULL, enqueued_at TEXT. Priority = triage score; claim is an atomic CAS on claimed_by.
schema.artifacts: ref TEXT PRIMARY KEY, appeal_id TEXT, scope TEXT, sha256 TEXT, ttl_expires_at TEXT, created_at TEXT. Backs FileStorePort; the TTL sweeper deletes expired rows + bytes (fixes PDFs-never-cleaned).

integrity_rules: All money is INTEGER micros/cents — never float (matches domain.money).
PHI columns store salted hashes only; raw PHI lives only in redacted_at_rest artifact bytes behind FileStorePort scope tokens.
audit + events + signoffs are append-only (no UPDATE/DELETE grants in the adapter).
Status transitions go through update_status_atomic (optimistic version CAS) — fixes the snapshot-watchdog race.
FILED requires (signoffs row inserted) AND (verify_chain()==True) AND (status CAS from AWAITING_SIGNOFF) in one transaction.
persistence.bounded_memory: MemoryAppealRepo (sim/fallback) is a bounded LRU with capacity + TTL eviction so it cannot OOM; SqliteAppealRepo has row caps + an eviction job for terminal appeals past retention.

security_model.auth: AuthPort (JwtAuthAdapter) enforces authentication on EVERY HTTP route and the WS handshake via a FastAPI dependency (get_principal) — fixes 'no auth on any endpoint' (Critical). RBAC authorize(principal, action, resource) gates per-appeal ownership for GET /appeals/{id}, /files, and the nurse queue — fixes 'unredacted GET /appeals' and '/files serves PHI unauthenticated' (Critical). A parametrized security test enumerates the whole route table so any new unguarded route fails CI.
security_model.phi_redaction_boundary: Structural: RedactionPort (LocalRedactionAdapter) is the SOLE producer of domain.RedactedText; every egress port (LetterRenderPort, EventBusPort/WS, AuditLogPort, FileStorePort, TtsPort, and the outbound side of LLMGatewayPort/RetrievalPort/ReasoningPort) accepts ONLY RedactedText for PHI-bearing fields, so unredacted PHI is a type error at the boundary. Runtime defense-in-depth: each egress adapter calls redaction.contains_phi() and refuses on a hit. The LLM gateway redacts on BOTH the outbound prompt and the inbound completion. Fixes: PHI-streamed-to-WS-unredacted, PHI-in-cleartext-PDFs, incomplete redact_phi (now hypothesis-fuzzed for member/NPI/SSN/DOB/claim patterns).
security_model.baa_gated_routing: Sponsors WITHOUT a BAA (MiniMax, Qwen/DashScope, Moss) sit strictly on the redacted side of the TrueFoundry boundary — the Service redacts via RedactionPort before any byte reaches them, and VoiceTurnService/RebuttalService assert PHI-clean before the call. PAVO and the ConcurrencyGate never receive PHI (telemetry + surrogate appeal_id only). The composition root wires these adapters so they are unreachable except through a redaction step.
security_model.tamper_evident_audit: AuditLogPort is a SHA-256 hash chain (each row's prev_hash = prior row's record_hash); verify_chain() recomputes and detects any field flip. The cryptographic sign-off gate (SignoffService) REQUIRES verify_chain()==True before SignaturePort.sign() and the atomic FILED transition; a broken chain raises and blocks filing. Audit stores hashes + token/cost metadata, never raw text. Sign-off is genuine Ed25519 over the redacted letter hash.
security_model.cors_csp_headers: infra/security_headers.py installs a CORS allowlist from Settings (NO wildcard — fixes 'wildcard CORS' Critical), a strict CSP (fixes the DOM-XSS surface in web/ alongside per-component output encoding), plus HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options=DENY, Referrer-Policy. WS upgrade checks Origin against the same allowlist (fixes 'no WS origin check' High).
security_model.path_traversal_fix: TWO layers: (1) UnsiloedDenialParserAdapter and the ingestion controller only ever accept in-memory validated bytes + a declared ArtifactKind — there is NO code path that opens a server-side filesystem path from user input (fixes 'arbitrary file read in EOB parse' Critical at the source). (2) LocalFileStoreAdapter canonicalizes every ref and jails it to BACKSTOP_ARTIFACT_DIR, rejecting '..' and absolute paths; reads require a signed scope token + ownership authz (fixes path traversal + the /files PHI exposure).
other_hardening: Upload size cap + content-type validation in ingestion_controller before buffering (fixes 'unbounded uploads', returns 413).
reportlab markup escaping of every free-text/PHI field in ReportlabLetterAdapter (fixes 'reportlab markup injection').
TaskSupervisorPort tracks every spawned task; FastAPI lifespan drains/cancels on shutdown (fixes 'fire-and-forget tasks' + 'no graceful shutdown').
ConcurrencyGatePort caps fan-out; AppealRepositoryPort is bounded (fixes 'no concurrency cap', 'threadpool starvation', 'unbounded APPEALS OOM').

infra/logging.py: structured JSON + PHI-scrubbing filter (fixes 'no structured logging'); infra/config.py fails fast on invalid config (fixes 'no config/validation'); pydantic schemas validate every payload (fixes 'no input validation').
Lock held only across in-memory mutation, never across a vendor await (fixes 'lock-scope serializes the swarm').

key_decisions: CHOSE Proposal #1 (layer-grouped hexagon) as the canonical tree, MERGING in Proposal #2's best ideas (PHI-as-a-type RedactedText, integer-cents Money/SolDeadline, audit+cost as shared ports every service consumes, the Appeal aggregate state machine encoding the cross-feature pipeline). Rationale: #1 literally matches the user's 'Controller->Service->Port->Adapter, one composition root' mandate, keeps one impure wiring file, and fits the existing orchestrator/backstop/ + pavo/router.py paths; #2's per-slice two-tier composition roots add file count and a shared-registry god-object risk without a payoff at hackathon scale. The product's bounded contexts are still honored as service files + domain aggregates, just under a technical-axis tree.

VERIFIED on disk: orchestrator/backstop/ does NOT exist yet — this is a GREENFIELD rebuild, not a refactor of running code. Only pavo-bench/ is present. Python is 3.9.6; torch 2.8.0 and numpy 2.0.2 are installed; sklearn is NOT. Decision: the Moss/MiniMax sim TF-IDF uses a stdlib RunbookCorpus util (sklearn optional accelerator) so CI has zero heavy ML deps and the torch-free numpy PAVO path stays clean.

VERIFIED + CORRECTED a flaw in the PAVO sponsor spec: the default checkpoint meta_controller_best.pt is a RAW state_dict, so load_pretrained returns info['architecture']==None. The spec's fail-fast guard `assert info['architecture']['n_profiles']==48` would CRASH. Corrected the M2 test_gate to assert info['n_params_loaded']==85041 (always present, verified) AND model.n_profiles==48. The dict-format meta_controller.pt does carry architecture={state_dim:12,hidden:256,n_profiles:48}.

VERIFIED PAVO numpy/torch bit-faithfulness empirically against the live checkpoint: 0 argmax mismatches over 2000 random 12-dim states, max abs logit error 1.9e-06, weight shapes W0[256,12]/W2[256,256]/W4[48,256]. This licenses NumpyPavoRoutingAdapter as BOTH the torch-free production fallback AND the canonical test double — it is the same frozen policy, not a degraded fake. PAVO is the one capability whose real and sim are policy-identical.

PHI redaction is enforced STRUCTURALLY: RedactionPort is the sole producer of RedactedText, and every egress port (LetterRender, EventBus/WS, AuditLog, FileStore, Tts, outbound LLM/Retrieval/Reasoning) accepts only RedactedText for PHI fields — making the six PHI-leak Critical/High vulns type errors at the boundary, with runtime contains_phi() defense-in-depth in each egress adapter.

TrueFoundry is split into FOUR single-responsibility ports (LLMGatewayPort, RedactionPort, AuditLogPort, CostLedgerPort) per the one-responsibility-per-file mandate; the gateway adapter is injected the same redaction/audit/cost singletons in both real and sim mode, so redaction + tamper-evident audit + priced cost are 100% real even in sim — only the upstream model proxy is stubbed (exactly the honesty contract).

Persistence is SQLite (WAL) behind AppealRepositoryPort/AuditLogPort/CostLedgerPort, replacing the unbounded global APPEALS dict; money stored as integer micros (no float); PHI columns are salted hashes only; audit/events/signoffs are append-only; FILED requires verify_chain()==True + Ed25519 signature + atomic status CAS in one transaction. The sim/test path uses a bounded LRU+TTL memory repo honoring the identical contract.

Every Critical/High audit vuln is mapped to a milestone test_gate: arbitrary-file-read+traversal (M8 bytes-only + M13 path-jail), no-auth+/files+GET-appeals (M13 AuthPort + M17 controllers), PHI-to-WS+PDF+incomplete-redact (M3 redaction + M13 EventBus/Letter), wildcard-CORS+WS-origin+CSP (M17), OOM+concurrency-cap+threadpool+lock-scope (M12+M15+M13 bounded repo), fire-and-forget+graceful-shutdown (M13 TaskSupervisor + M17 lifespan), reportlab-injection (M13), snapshot-race (M13 atomic CAS), structured-logging+config+validation (M0/M17), DOM-XSS (M17 web/).
